      "observations": [
        "All 508 owned diff lines across seven paths were read. All product/conditional metadata was checked first. mailnews.js contains unrelated Suite branches, but both changed hunk ranges and the needed OAuth preferences are outside them; those unrelated bodies are excluded. The patch also removes stray RFC-comment punctuation and distinguishes external-localhost from external-net-thunderbird telemetry.",
        "The owned selection keeps the general external-browser flag with an HTTP-loopback check, then adds a sibling custom-scheme branch using useNetThunderbirdRedirect plus the redirect protocol. Its new preference defaults false and only the test issuer gains that scheme. The literal review request to nest the new branch inside useExternalBrowser is not adopted. The author later objects that provider URL and preference must agree, proposes moving the decision to providers, then ships anyway. Neither that proposal nor the ship-anyway rationale is a source guarantee of no effects.",
        "URLCallbackRequest registers itself by the generated authorization state. The owned observer accepts the topic and /callback path, then dispatches only to an existing state entry. urlReceived deletes that entry before finishAuthorizationRequest and onAuthorizationReceived. The request opens the system browser and returns true; its close method is empty. Finishing clears request/connection state but does not itself clear that static callback map. This is a bounded cleanup contract, not a reproduced leak, cancellation failure or security proof.",
        "The actual accepted command-line caller routes the scheme by URL host through the category manager. Its OAuth registration now contains oauth/oauth2; the handler has later path checks for callback/yahoo. The original only registers oauth2 and checks /callback. A direct service observer call bypasses the command-line/category delivery step, so observer acceptance is not an operating-system scheme-routing test.",
        "Exact whole current objects from 5334 and 5292 are reused after pinned revision/blob/line-byte checks. Later accepted source uses schemeRedirect, useSchemeRedirect and an OS default-client query, distinct from the owned redirect-endpoint/pref design and TODO. The current false-or-true default is conditional on MOZ_ESR; do not transfer it to the owned false default. Later issuer checks and cancellation guards are separate source phases, not outcomes of this landing.",
        "The parameterized owned success tests directly assert SASL token, in-memory tokens, scope, persisted login fields and transport telemetry for both cases. The helper's custom-scheme path generates a callback and calls observe directly; loopback still uses HTTP redirect. The extracted getRedirectURL retains state/scope/one-time code behavior but removes the old fake-server username/password comparison. This narrows what the fixture can prove. The existing mismatched-state test remains a loopback case; no new custom-scheme invalid-state or cancellation scenario is added.",
        "Changed assertion messages are nonempty, but the modified helper's code_challenge_method comparison has no message in its affected context. The invalid-scheme diagnostic names net.net-thunderbird instead of net.thunderbird. The owned URLCallbackRequest constructor summary incorrectly says internal browser while start opens externally; accepted source later corrects that summary. isNetThunderbirdRedirect can return null for an invalid URL although its JSDoc says boolean, and its caller uses truthiness. These scoped comment/message findings do not create global rules or runtime failures.",
        "No authentication, OS registration/default-client action, network, browser, telemetry collection or test ran. Historical provider verification is attributed to its reporter, and no external service, native scheme delivery, hostile URI or cancellation behavior is independently validated.",
        "Full primary Bug 2033653 is locally reconciled from B's current 0–2/activity/footer capture. The earlier scheme dependency 2024725 is a locator; only the actual necessary current command-line/category receiver is inspected here. No live provider, OS delivery or authentication confirmation is claimed.",
        "Full D297815 includes all three actual bodies 1621886/1621899/1621964. The literal 1621886 nesting request puts custom-scheme routing inside lazy.useExternalBrowser; owned source keeps it as a sibling branch, and Not Done is retained. The clicked-URL wording nit and author reply are narrower: the owned method documentation now says redirected. Done is not used as implementation proof.",
        "The review first questions whether providers can be tested, then reports Microsoft configuration working and proposes enabling the preference or shipping a separate change. The author later objects that redirect endpoint and preference must agree, proposes moving the preference decision into providers, and explicitly ships anyway. The owned false preference and test issuer remain distinct from those suggestions and the later accepted schemeRedirect/capability design. The no-effect rationale is a historical author statement, not a guarantee about test-fixture or telemetry effects.",
        "The source directly checks state registration/lookup/deletion order, empty close, request completion, actual host-category delivery and the simulated observer callback. Test success assertions cover tokens/login/transport telemetry but not OS handler delivery, custom-scheme invalid-state or cancel lifecycle. Removed fake-server credential comparison and scoped comment/assertion defects remain explicit. Current source reuses exact original 5334/5292 objects/times; no new independent confirmation or runtime result."
